newsitem.title: USA: Lucent's Octel deal praised, but charge hurts.
newsitem.headline: Lucent's Octel deal praised, but charge hurts.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc's agreement to acquire Octel Communications Corp for $1.8 billion drew early investor praise that was tempered by an unspecified charge that sparked a selloff in Lucent stock.

Arbitrageurs and traders said they agreed with the deal's rationale, the expansion of Lucent's voice processing systems including messaging, which will create a strong rival to competitor Northern Telecom Ltd, among others.
"The deal makes sense. Octel has been struggling, trading between 20 to 30 forever, and Lucent is a fabulous buyer," said an arb who requested anonimity.
"They are calling the deal neutral (to earnings in the first year), but there is a significant charge, so Lucent stock should get knocked around a little bit," a second arb said.
Lucent said it will pay $31 cash for each Octel share.
In Thursday morning trade, Octel shares jumped 3-3/4, or 14 percent, to 30-1/2 while Lucent slumped 3-5/16, or 3.7 percent, to 85-3/8.
In the deal's announcement, Lucent said the acquisition would result in a "significant one-time, non-cash charge against its earnings" related to the write-off of in-process research and development.

The unspecified charge will be taken in the fourth quarter, and is expected to "have a significant effect on net earnings for the fourth fiscal quarter of 1997 as well as the company's net earnings for the fiscal year ending September 30 1997.
"It looks like a straightforward tender (offer), a clean, plain vanilla deal," a third arb said.

The deal is expected to be completed by the end of August and is expected to be neutral to earnings in the first full year of operation and additive to earnings thereafter, Lucent said in a statement.
